source: KSQAAC Spardha Yashassu NMMS study material 2022 (NMMS.pdf), SAT section: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology), Social Science and Maths questions with the book's answer keys, read from the rendered pages.

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The figure that shows the minimum work done is

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Force, Motion and Energy: work = force × displacement × cos θ, where θ is the angle between them
steps: A: θ = 180°, W = −Fs (negative)
The least value is −Fs, in A

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt:
Statement (A): A mixer bowl gets heated when the mixer is used for a few minutes.
Reason (R): The mixer bowl is heated by the heat produced by friction.

options.A: R is the right reason for statement A
options.B: R is not the right reason for statement A
options.C: Statement A is not at all related to reason R
options.D: Statement A is wrong, reason R is right

solution.concept: 5.4 Friction acts between surfaces rubbing over each other, and it produces heat
steps: The blades and the contents rub against each other and the bowl, so friction heats the bowl
A is true and R explains it

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: A person carries a 14 kg LPG cylinder up the steps to the first floor, 12 m high. The work done is (g = 10 m/s²)

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Force, Motion and Energy: work done against gravity = m × g × h

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: A research institute selected 4 liquids P, Q, R and S for generating electricity from ocean heat energy. Their boiling points are 200 K, 150 K, 210 K and 145 K respectively. The liquid best suited for turning the turbine is

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Force, Motion and Energy: ocean thermal energy: the warm surface water boils a liquid with a low boiling point, and its vapour turns the turbine
steps: The lower the boiling point, the more easily the liquid turns to vapour
S boils at the lowest temperature, 145 K

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: A child is playing on a swing. The potential energy is maximum

options.A: when the swing is at the middle point
options.B: when the swing is moving from the back to the middle point
options.C: when the swing is at its greatest height, in front or at the back
options.D: when the swing is at rest

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Force, Motion and Energy: potential energy = m × g × h grows with height
steps: The swing is highest at the ends of its path, in front or at the back
So its potential energy is greatest there

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: A refrigerator used 96 kWh of electricity in a month (30 days), running 8 hours a day. Its power is

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Force, Motion and Energy: power = energy used ÷ time taken
steps: Time = 8 × 30 = 240 hours
Power = 96 kWh ÷ 240 h = 0.4 kW = 400 W

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The situation in which work is done is

options.A: a hand is moved round in a circle

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Force, Motion and Energy: work is done when a force moves an object in the direction of the force
steps: Pushing a book applies a force that moves the book along the push
So work is done on the book

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: When a cart of mass 15 kg is pushed with an acceleration of 2 m/s², it moves a distance of 50 m. The work done is
questions.note: Work = force × distance = (15 × 2) × 50 = 1500 J, which is 1.5 kJ, and no option says that. The options were probably meant in joules (then the answer is 1500 J), but the book’s key gives A, 15 kJ. This waits for a corrected version.

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: Spheres A, B and C are at heights of 5 m, 4 m and 6 m respectively. Their potential energies in ascending order are (g = 10 m/s²)

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Force, Motion and Energy: potential energy = m × g × h
steps: Ascending: A (50), C (180), B (200)

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: A student playing in a field hears a plane flying in the sky and looks up at it. The lens in his eye

options.D: is not affected by the distance of the object

solution.concept: 10.4 The convex lens in the human eye changes its shape to focus objects at different distances
steps: To focus a far-away object the eye lens becomes thinner, so its curvature decreases
The book’s key gives A (increases), but that is what happens for a near object

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: Two plane mirrors are arranged as shown in the figure. An object is placed between them. The number of images formed is

solution.concept: 11.8 Mirrors placed at an angle give many images by repeated reflection: 360° ÷ angle − 1 of them
steps: The mirrors are at 90°

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The distance between a student standing in front of a plane mirror and his image is 50 cm. How far is the student from the mirror?

solution.concept: 11.5 A plane mirror forms the image as far behind the mirror as the object is in front of it
steps: Student-to-image distance = 2 × student-to-mirror distance

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: A train passes at high speed in front of a student standing on a railway platform. The train and the writing on it look blurred to the student. The reason for this is

options.B: The image of the train is formed on the blind spot of the retina
options.C: The image of the train on the retina changes in less than 1/16 of a second
options.D: The image of the train on the retina changes more slowly than once in 1/16 of a second

solution.concept: Beyond the syllabus: persistence of vision: an image stays on the retina for about 1/16 of a second
steps: The fast train’s image moves on before the last one has faded
The images overlap, so the train and its writing look blurred

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: Which of these capital letters of the English alphabet looks exactly the same in a plane mirror?

solution.concept: 11.5 A plane mirror inverts left and right, so only letters that are the same on both sides of a vertical line look unchanged
steps: M is the same on both sides of its middle line
Q, C and D are not, so their images are reversed

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: A man stands 4 m from a plane mirror. If the distance between his image and the mirror is to be 10 m, the man should
questions.note: As printed, the image must be 10 m behind the mirror, so the man must stand 10 m in front of it and move 6 m back, which no option gives. The book’s key, D (move 1 m back), fits if the 10 m is the distance between the man and his image (5 m from the mirror). This waits for a corrected version.

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: If you get a chance to watch cricket in a large cricket stadium, which of the following devices would you like to use?

solution.concept: 10.4 Lenses are used in telescopes; binoculars are a pair of small telescopes, one for each eye
steps: A player across a big stadium is far away, but not as far as the stars
Binoculars magnify far objects and are easy to hold and use with both eyes

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: White light splits into colours (disperses) when it passes through a prism. The colours that bend the most and the least are, respectively,

solution.concept: Beyond the syllabus: dispersion: a prism bends each colour of white light by a different amount
steps: The spectrum runs VIBGYOR from the most bent to the least bent
Violet bends the most and red the least

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The instrument that can be made from broken pieces of a plane mirror is a

solution.concept: 11.8 A kaleidoscope is made of three plane mirror strips joined into a triangle
steps: Strips cut from a broken plane mirror are enough to make a kaleidoscope
The others need lenses

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The fluorescent object among the following is
questions.note: The Sun, fire and an electric bulb all give out their own light (luminous) and the Moon does not, but none of them is “fluorescent” in the usual sense (a tube light is). The book’s key gives D, which can’t be checked as the question is worded.

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The colour that does not appear in a rainbow is

solution.concept: Beyond the syllabus: a rainbow shows the seven colours of white light: violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, red
steps: Red, indigo and blue are among the seven
Pink is not; the book’s key gives C (indigo), which is one of the seven

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The capital letter “T” is placed in front of a plane mirror. Its image looks like
questions.note: The book prints the second option’s label as “D)”; it is option B.

solution.concept: 11.5 A plane mirror inverts left and right; letters like A, H, I, M, T look the same
steps: T is the same on both sides of its upright line
Its image is an upright T, as in A

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: Which of the following figures illustrates the first law of reflection of light?

solution.concept: 10.3 First law of reflection: the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection
steps: In D both rays make 35° with the mirror, so both make 55° with the normal
In A and B the angles differ (55° and 35°); in C one 35° is from the mirror and the other from the normal

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: A boy is riding a bicycle on a road. The frictional force that the wheel exerts on the road is

solution.concept: 5.3 Forces act in pairs between two objects, and 5.4 friction acts between surfaces in contact
steps: As the wheel turns, its grip pushes the road backwards
The road pushes the wheel forwards by the same friction, which drives the bicycle on

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The front of an aeroplane is pointed. This

options.A: reduces the weight of the aeroplane
options.B: reduces the friction due to air

solution.concept: 5.4 Air and water also exert friction (drag), so aeroplanes, ships, birds and fish have streamlined shapes
steps: A pointed, streamlined front lets the air flow past smoothly
That reduces air friction

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: We slip when walking barefoot on ice. This is because

options.A: surface of ice provides more friction
options.B: surface of ice provides less friction
options.C: bare feet are smooth, so they slip
options.D: we are not used to walking on ice

solution.concept: 5.4 Friction depends on how rough the surfaces in contact are
steps: The surface of ice is very smooth
It gives very little friction, so the foot slips

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: Smitha rolls a toy car on a dry marble floor, a wet marble floor, newspaper and a towel spread on the floor. The frictional force on the car, in increasing order, is

options.A: wet marble floor, dry marble floor, newspaper, towel
options.B: newspaper, towel, dry marble floor, wet marble floor
options.C: towel, newspaper, dry marble floor, wet marble floor
options.D: wet marble floor, dry marble floor, towel, newspaper

solution.concept: 5.4 The smoother the surface, the less the friction
steps: Wet marble is the smoothest, then dry marble, then newspaper; a towel is the roughest
Increasing friction: wet marble, dry marble, newspaper, towel

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The two forces that act everywhere around us are

solution.concept: 5.4 Gravity pulls every object towards the Earth, and friction acts wherever surfaces touch
steps: Everything around us is pulled down by gravity and rests or moves on some surface
Magnetic and electrostatic forces act only near magnets or charged objects

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The friction caused by fluids depends on

solution.concept: 5.4 Fluid friction (drag) depends on the speed, the shape of the object and the fluid
steps: Faster motion and a blunter shape mean more drag, and it differs from fluid to fluid
So it depends on all three

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: A horse has to pull harder to start a cart moving. The reason is

options.A: friction before motion starts (limiting friction) is greater than friction during motion
options.B: sliding friction is greater than rolling friction
options.C: no force acts while the cart is still
options.D: air friction is greater at the start

solution.concept: 5.4 Friction acts when an object moves or tries to move over a surface
steps: The friction to be overcome to start motion is greater than the friction once it moves
So the horse pulls harder at the start

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: A boy hears the echo of his shout after 4 seconds. The distance of the reflecting object from the boy is (speed of sound 346 m/s)

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Sound: an echo travels to the object and back, so distance = speed × time ÷ 2
steps: The book leaves out the speed of sound; its answer uses 346 m/s (air at about 25 °C)
Distance = 346 × 4 ÷ 2 = 692 m

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: A moving vehicle sounds its horn. The horn sounds stronger in front of the vehicle than behind it. This is because

options.A: the frequency of the sound is higher in front than behind
options.B: the amplitude of the sound is higher in front and lower behind
options.C: the wavelength of the sound is longer in front and shorter behind
options.D: the amplitude is higher in front and the frequency is higher behind

questions.note: In front of a moving source the sound waves are bunched up (the Doppler effect), so their frequency is higher (A), but the question asks why the sound is stronger, which is about amplitude (B). The book’s key gives A; as worded, the question has no single answer.

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: A sound has a larger amplitude and so is louder. Because of this

options.C: it fades as the distance increases
options.D: it can be heard from farther away

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Sound: the larger the amplitude, the louder the sound
steps: A louder sound carries more energy
So it can be heard from a greater distance

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: We hear a mosquito’s wings vibrating as it flies, but we can’t see the vibrations. This is because

options.A: the wings have a long wavelength
options.B: the wings vibrate at a high frequency
options.C: the wings have a long time period
options.D: the wings have a large amplitude

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Sound: frequency is the number of vibrations per second
steps: A mosquito’s wings vibrate hundreds of times a second
That is too fast for the eye to follow, yet it is in the range we hear

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: Four states with different temperatures are given. In which of them is the speed of sound generally the lowest?
questions.note: Sound travels more slowly in colder air, so the answer is the coldest place, not Rajasthan (the book’s key, B), where it is fastest. Kargil (C) and Jammu and Kashmir (A) are both cold, and Kargil was part of Jammu and Kashmir when the book was written, so the question has no single answer.

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: A wave of wavelength 20 cm makes 10 compressions and 11 rarefactions. The distance it travels is

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Sound: one wavelength holds one compression and one rarefaction
steps: 10 compressions means 10 whole waves (the extra rarefaction is where it started)
Distance = 10 × 20 = 200 cm

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: A school bell makes a sound of frequency 4 kHz and wavelength 10 cm. How long does the sound take to reach a student 1 km from the school?

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Sound: speed of a wave = frequency × wavelength

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: One of the main reasons for fitting silencers to vehicles is

options.C: to decrease the amplitude of sound
options.D: to maintain the quality of sound

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Sound: loudness depends on amplitude; silencers reduce noise pollution
steps: A silencer lowers the amplitude of the engine’s sound
So the vehicle is quieter

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: A musician is singing. The feature of his voice that does not change is its

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Sound: quality (timbre) is what makes each person’s voice their own
steps: While singing, his loudness and pitch go up and down
The quality of his voice stays the same, which is how we recognise it

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: A harsh sound is repeated at regular intervals. The sound then becomes

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Sound: musical sounds are regular (periodic); noise is irregular
steps: A sound repeated at regular intervals is periodic
Periodic sound is heard as music (a rhythm)

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: A musician sings at a high pitch. His voice then

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Sound: pitch depends on frequency; a high pitch sounds shrill
steps: A high pitch means a high frequency
High-frequency sound is shrill

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The vibrations of some objects can’t be seen. This is because

options.A: the amplitude of vibrations is high
options.B: the frequency of vibrations is low
options.C: the time period of vibrations is low
options.D: the amplitude of vibrations is low

questions.note: Two options explain it: vibrations too small to see (D, the book’s key) and vibrations too fast to follow, which is what a short time period (C) means (question 33 gives that reason for a mosquito’s wings). So the question has no single answer.

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: Car X starts from A, goes on to C and then comes back to stop at B. Car Y starts from A and stops at B. Which statement about them is true?

options.A: The displacement of X is more than that of Y
options.B: The displacements of the two cars are the same
options.C: The displacement of Y is half that of X
options.D: The displacement of X is half that of Y

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Force, Motion and Energy: displacement is the straight-line distance from the start to the end point, whatever the path
steps: Both cars start at A and end at B
So their displacements are the same, AB, though X travelled farther

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: An ox walks round a circle of radius 2 m. After three and a half rounds, the distance it has travelled and its displacement are

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Force, Motion and Energy: distance is the length of the path; displacement is the straight line from start to end
steps: After half a round more it is opposite the start: displacement = diameter = 4 m

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: A girl whirls a stone tied to a string round in a circle at a steady rate. The stone

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Force, Motion and Energy: velocity has a direction as well as a size (speed)
steps: Going round steadily, the stone keeps the same speed
Its direction keeps changing, so its velocity changes (B is wrong) and its acceleration turns with it (C is wrong)
The book’s key gives B

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: Which statement about the motion of bodies A and B in the graph is correct?

options.C: A moves with non-uniform speed and B with uniform speed

questions.note: A’s curve gets steeper, so its speed increases (A is true). B is a straight line, so its speed is uniform, not decreasing (B is false), which makes C true and D (“all of the above”) false. Two options are true, so the question has no single answer; the book’s key gives D.

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The force needed to throw an iron ball of mass 2 kg to a distance of 5 m is
questions.note: The force can’t be found from the mass and the distance alone: it depends on how long the push lasts and at what angle the ball is thrown. The book’s key gives B (10 N, which is 2 × 5), but force is not mass × distance.

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The Moon seems to change its shape every day, and at times only half of it is seen. The reason is that

options.C: the Moon does not give out its own light

solution.concept: 11.1 The Moon has no light of its own; we see the part of its sunlit half that faces the Earth
steps: The Sun always lights one half of the Moon
As the Moon goes round the Earth we see different parts of that lit half, so its shape seems to change

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The Moon takes less time to go once round the Earth than it takes to go from one full moon (or new moon) to the next. The cause of this difference is

options.B: the motion of the Earth in its orbit
options.C: the pull of the Earth’s gravity on the Moon

questions.note: The book gives the times as 29.53 days and 30 days; they are about 27.3 days (one round) and 29.5 days (full moon to full moon), so the numbers are left out here.

solution.concept: 11.1 The phases repeat once the Moon is again on the same side of the Earth as seen from the Sun
steps: While the Moon goes round the Earth, the Earth moves along its own orbit round the Sun
So the Moon must go a little further before Sun, Earth and Moon line up again

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: Seasons occur on the Earth because of

options.A: the rotation and revolution of the Earth
options.B: the rotation of the Earth and the tilt of its axis
options.C: the rotation of the Earth and the Moon
options.D: the attraction between the Earth and the Sun

questions.note: Seasons are caused by the Earth’s revolution round the Sun together with the tilt of its axis. Option A leaves out the tilt and option B (the book’s key) has rotation instead of revolution, so no option is right.

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The Pole Star does not seem to move because

options.B: it lies in line with the Earth’s axis
options.C: it is too far away for its motion to be seen
options.D: it can’t be seen against the other stars

questions.note: The book says “in line with the Earth’s latitude”; it means the Earth’s axis.

solution.concept: 12.1 The Earth rotates about its axis, and the Pole Star lies almost exactly above the North Pole, on that axis
steps: Stars seem to turn round the sky because the Earth rotates
A star on the line of the axis stays in the same place

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: Celestial bodies seem to move from east to west across the sky because

options.A: they move from east to west
options.B: the Earth rotates from west to east
options.C: the Earth moves from east to west
options.D: of the Earth’s rotation and revolution

solution.concept: 12.1 The Earth rotates from west to east, so the Sun, Moon and stars seem to move from east to west
steps: As we turn eastward with the Earth, the sky seems to slide the other way
So the bodies seem to rise in the east and set in the west

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: Which list gives the planets in descending order of size?

solution.concept: 13.1 The planets differ in size: Saturn is a giant; Earth is a little bigger than Venus; Mars is about half Earth’s size
steps: Diameters: Saturn about 1,20,000 km, Earth 12,756 km, Venus 12,104 km, Mars 6,792 km
Descending: Saturn, Earth, Venus, Mars; the book’s key gives B, which puts Mars before Venus

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The surface of still water acts like a mirror. This is because

options.A: the surface of water is horizontal
options.B: the water surface turns back (reflects) light
options.C: the surface of water lets light pass through

solution.concept: 11.5 Reflection is the change in the direction of light when it falls on a shiny surface
steps: A still water surface is smooth and shiny
It reflects light, so it forms images like a mirror

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The mirror a student can use to see a wide area is

solution.concept: 10.2 A convex mirror always gives an erect, smaller image and a much wider field of view
steps: That is why vehicles use convex mirrors as rear-view mirrors
So a convex mirror shows the widest area

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: Grains in boiling water move up and down. This is because of

options.A: the grains being less dense than water

solution.concept: 7.2 Convection: heated water rises and cooler water sinks, setting up currents
steps: Water at the bottom is heated, rises, cools and sinks again
These convection currents carry the grains up and down

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: Person A stands on loose sand. Person B, of the same mass, lies on the same sand. In this case

options.A: A and B apply different forces on the sand
options.B: A exerts more pressure on the sand
options.C: B exerts more pressure on the sand
options.D: A and B exert the same pressure on the sand

solution.concept: 6.1 Pressure = force ÷ area: the same force on a smaller area gives more pressure
steps: Both press on the sand with the same force, their weight (so A is wrong)
Standing, A’s feet cover a much smaller area, so A exerts more pressure; the book’s key gives A

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: It is dangerous to stand close to the edge of a platform when a train passes at high speed. This is because

options.A: the fast-moving air lowers the pressure, and the person is pushed towards the train
options.B: the fast-moving air raises the pressure and pushes the person away
options.C: the person may slip onto the track
options.D: the fast-moving air raises the pressure and pulls the person in

solution.concept: 6.4 High-speed winds lower the air pressure
steps: The train drags air along with it at high speed, so the pressure between the person and the train drops
The higher pressure of the still air behind the person pushes them towards the train

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: In which situation is work done?

options.C: A person standing with luggage on his head
options.D: Pushing a toy car forward by hand

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Force, Motion and Energy: work is done only when a force moves an object
steps: Pushing a wall or holding a load still moves nothing
The pushed toy car moves along the push, so work is done

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: An empty oil tin is half filled with water, which is boiled for 10 minutes. The tin is then closed with its lid and cold water is poured over it. The tin suddenly gets crushed because

options.A: the pressure inside drops, and the air pressure outside crushes it
options.B: of the pressure of the water vapour
options.C: the tin becomes thin when heated

solution.concept: 6.2 The air around us presses on everything with atmospheric pressure
steps: Boiling fills the tin with steam; cold water makes the steam condense, leaving very little gas inside
The air pressure outside is now much greater and crushes the tin; the book’s key gives C

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: Gases can be compressed easily, but water can’t. The reason is

options.A: there is no gap between water molecules
options.C: the repulsion between the molecules is greater than the pressure

solution.concept: 7.3 In a liquid the particles are already very close together; in a gas they are far apart
steps: Pushed closer, liquid particles repel each other strongly, more than an ordinary pressure can overcome
There are small gaps between water molecules, so A (and so D) is wrong

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: Two pieces of wood lean against a wall as shown in the figure, one touching it with face A and the other with side B. In this case

options.A: face A exerts more pressure on the wall
options.B: side B exerts more pressure on the wall
options.D: face A applies more force on the wall

questions.note: The book’s key, B, needs side B to touch the wall over a smaller area than face A, but the figure shows both pieces touching the wall the same way, so the question can’t be checked as printed.

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: A red-hot piece of charcoal bursts into flame when air is blown on it. This is because of

options.A: air being pulled towards the charcoal
options.C: the pressure round the charcoal dropping as air flows in from all sides

questions.note: Blowing makes charcoal flare up because it brings in more fresh air, and so more oxygen for burning. None of the options says that; the book’s key gives C.

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: Porter A puts a round cloth pad 20 cm across on his head, and porter B one 10 cm across. If both carry loads of the same mass on their heads,

options.A: the pressure on B is more
options.B: the force on B is more
options.C: the pressure on both is the same
options.D: the pressure on A is more

solution.concept: 6.1 Pressure = force ÷ area; porters use a folded round cloth to spread the load
steps: The force (the load’s weight) is the same on both
B’s pad has a smaller area, so the pressure on B’s head is more

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: When a bullet is fired from a gun,

options.A: the gun gets the same acceleration as the bullet, in the opposite direction
options.B: the gun gets the same acceleration as the bullet, in the same direction
options.C: the gun gets the same momentum as the bullet, in the opposite direction
options.D: the gun gets the same momentum as the bullet, in the same direction

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Force, Motion and Energy: action and reaction are equal and opposite, so the total momentum stays zero
steps: Before firing, gun and bullet are at rest: total momentum 0
Afterwards the gun’s momentum must be equal and opposite to the bullet’s; the heavy gun moves back slowly, so its acceleration is much smaller

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Sachin added acetic acid and potassium hydroxide to two separate test tubes containing phenolphthalein. The colours seen in the test tubes are

solution.concept: 2.1 Indicators show acids and bases by colour; phenolphthalein stays colourless in acids and turns pink in bases
steps: Acetic acid is an acid: colourless
Potassium hydroxide is a base: pink

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: A student touched a solution in the chemistry lab and it felt soapy. The solution is

solution.concept: 2.1 Bases feel soapy or slippery to touch
steps: A solution that feels soapy is basic (alkaline)

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Vibha added turmeric powder and baking soda to cake batter. The red colour that forms shows the presence of

solution.concept: 2.1 Turmeric turns red in a basic solution
steps: Baking soda is a base, so the turmeric in the batter turns red

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: What should be added to alkaline soil to get a good yield?

solution.concept: 2.3 Soil that is too basic is treated with organic matter (manure or compost), which releases acids
steps: Compost neutralises the excess base
Quicklime and slaked lime are bases, used for acidic soil

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Turmeric powder turns red when added to lime water because

solution.concept: 2.1 Turmeric turns red in a basic solution; lime water is calcium hydroxide, a base
steps: So turmeric in lime water turns red

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Which pair reacts to give a salt and water?

options.D: Lime water and milk of magnesia

solution.concept: 2.2 Neutralisation: acid + base → salt + water
steps: Lemon juice (citric acid) and sodium hydroxide (a base) neutralise each other
The other pairs are not an acid with a base

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Doctors give medicine containing magnesium hydroxide to a person with acidity and indigestion because

options.A: it neutralises the alcohol in the stomach
options.B: it neutralises the hydrochloric acid in the stomach
options.C: it stops the enzymes in the stomach working
options.D: it oxidises glucose in the intestine

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Red litmus paper is dipped into lemon juice, distilled water and lime water. The colours of the paper are, respectively,

steps: Lemon juice (acid): red; distilled water (neutral): red; lime water (base): blue

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: A student concludes that curd is acidic because

Methyl orange turning red shows an acid

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: An indicator is made by soaking red hibiscus petals in water. The colours it shows with an acid and with a base are, respectively,

solution.concept: 2.1 Flower indicators such as red rose and red hibiscus turn a shade of red (dark pink) in acids and green in bases

The book’s key gives B, the other way round

questions.subject: chemistry

Distilled water is pure and hardly conducts, so the bulb won’t glow; the book’s key gives C (milk)

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: The main purpose of coating iron with tin is that

questions.subject: chemistry

The electrolyte is a solution of a copper salt, copper sulphate

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Workers in the steel and mining industries suffer the most lung diseases. One of the main causes is

solution.concept: 13.6 Pollution is one of the threats to life on Earth; fine particles in the air harm the lungs
steps: Breathing in fine ash and dust particles day after day damages the lungs
Radiation, water and detergents don’t act on the lungs

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: To supply germ-free drinking water to homes at low cost, the chemical to add to the water is

solution.concept: 4.5 Chlorine is used to purify water; bleaching powder (calcium oxychloride) gives out chlorine
steps: Bleaching powder is cheap and kills germs in drinking water
The other calcium compounds don’t disinfect

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: If the number of E. coli (Escherichia coli) bacteria in river water is very high,

options.D: the water is not fit for farming

solution.concept: 3.4 Many diseases spread through water polluted with sewage
steps: E. coli bacteria live in the intestines of mammals
Many of them in river water show that faeces (sewage) have got into it

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: The correct statement about the ozone layer is

options.A: Ozone is made of three oxygen atoms and is found in the mesosphere
options.B: It makes the Earth look blue by refracting sunlight
options.C: The ozone layer can be built up by using more DDT
options.D: The ozone layer is thinning because of the use of chlorofluorocarbons

solution.concept: 13.6 The Montreal Protocol phased out chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) so that the ozone layer could recover
steps: CFCs destroy ozone, so their use thinned the ozone layer
Ozone is in the stratosphere (not the mesosphere), and DDT does not enrich it

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Sarala notices that the bottoms of her cooking pots turn black. The fuel that would solve this problem is

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Combustion and Flame: fuels that burn completely give no soot; incomplete burning leaves black carbon
steps: The black on the utensils is soot from a fuel that does not burn completely
LPG burns with a clean blue flame and is the usual cooking gas

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: The safest clothes to wear while cooking are made of

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Synthetic Fibres and Plastics: synthetic fibres melt when heated and stick to the body; cotton does not
steps: Nylon, polyester and rayon-type clothes can melt or catch fire easily in the kitchen
Cotton is the safe choice

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: The central government urges people to buy electric vehicles because

options.A: electric vehicles need no energy source
options.B: electric vehicles can run on fossil fuels
options.C: electricity is easy to produce and store

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Coal and Petroleum: fossil fuels are exhaustible: they took millions of years to form and are running out
steps: Electric vehicles reduce the use of petrol and diesel
That saves fossil fuels, which are running out

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Petroleum is called black gold because,

options.A: petroleum products burn with black smoke
options.B: many useful petrochemicals are obtained from petroleum
options.C: petroleum products pollute the environment when burnt

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Coal and Petroleum: petroleum gives many useful substances (petrochemicals), so it is called black gold
steps: Petrol, diesel, wax, plastics and many other products come from petroleum
That is why it is so valuable

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: The group made up of coal products is

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Coal and Petroleum: processing coal gives coke, coal tar and coal gas
steps: Petrol, diesel, grease, LPG, kerosene and paraffin come from petroleum
Coke, coal gas and tar come from coal

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Fractional distillation works because the components have different

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Coal and Petroleum: petroleum is refined by fractional distillation
steps: Its parts boil at different temperatures, so they separate as the vapour rises and cools

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Kerosene is better than petrol for oil lamps because it is

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Coal and Petroleum: petrol evaporates (is volatile) much more easily than kerosene
steps: Petrol in an open lamp would evaporate quickly and catch fire dangerously
Kerosene is less volatile, so it burns steadily and safely

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: The gas in an LPG cylinder is turned into a liquid by

solution.concept: 7.3 Gas particles are far apart, so pressing them together turns a gas into a liquid
steps: LPG is stored as a liquid by compressing the gas (raising its pressure) into the cylinder

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: The substance that comes out first when an oil well is drilled through the rocks is

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Coal and Petroleum: natural gas lies above the petroleum in an oil well
steps: When the rocks are drilled through, the natural gas on top comes out first

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: The beam of light going to the screen in a cinema hall can be seen because it is scattered. This is the

solution.concept: Beyond the syllabus: the Tyndall effect: tiny particles scatter a beam of light and make its path visible
steps: Dust and smoke particles in the cinema hall scatter the projector’s beam
That is the Tyndall effect

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Which element has the same electronic configuration as Ca²⁺?

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Structure of the Atom: an ion with the same number of electrons as a noble gas has its electronic configuration
steps: Calcium has 20 electrons; Ca²⁺ has lost 2, leaving 18
Argon has 18 electrons (2, 8, 8)

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: The Na⁺ ion has the same number of electrons as

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Structure of the Atom: isoelectronic particles have the same number of electrons
steps: Na⁺ has 11 − 1 = 10 electrons
Mg²⁺ has 12 − 2 = 10; Li⁺ has 2, Ca²⁺ 18, Ba²⁺ 54

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: The group of elements that have isotopes is

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: A non-metal burns in oxygen to give a gas. The gas dissolves in water to form a solution that turns blue litmus red. The non-metal is

solution.concept: 4.3 Non-metal oxides dissolve in water to form acids, which turn blue litmus red

Gallium is a metal; germanium and silicon are metalloids whose oxides don’t dissolve to give acids

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Household mirrors are coated with silver or aluminium at the back. This gives the mirror

solution.concept: 4.1 Metals have lustre: their surfaces are shiny
steps: A shiny silver or aluminium layer gives the mirror its reflecting surface

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: A metal X reacts with dilute H₂SO₄ to give a gas Y, which burns with a pop sound. X and Y are

solution.concept: 4.3 Metals react with dilute acids to give hydrogen, which burns with a pop

Zinc reacts with dilute sulphuric acid to give it; copper does not react

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: A drinking water source near a residential area has germs in it. The element used to make it safe to drink is

solution.concept: 4.5 Chlorine is a non-metal widely used in water purification
steps: Chlorine kills the germs and makes the water safe to drink

questions.subject: chemistry

solution.concept: Beyond the syllabus: gallium (about 30 °C) and caesium (about 28 °C) melt at the lowest temperatures among metals other than mercury

Potassium, sodium and lithium melt at about 64 °C, 98 °C and 180 °C

questions.subject: chemistry

solution.concept: 4.2 Galvanisation coats iron with a thin layer of zinc to stop rusting
steps: Zinc is more reactive (more electropositive) than iron
So zinc reacts with air and moisture first and protects the iron, even where the coat is scratched

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: A gas used to keep food fried in oil fresh for a long time is

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Food Preservation: packets of fried food are filled with nitrogen so that the oil does not go rancid

Nitrogen is unreactive and pushes the oxygen out

questions.subject: chemistry

It would react with the acids in food, so cans are coated with less reactive tin

questions.subject: chemistry

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Silver is a good conductor of electricity, but it is not used for household wiring because it is

solution.concept: 4.1 Silver is the best conductor of electricity, but it is a precious metal
steps: Silver costs far more than copper, so copper is used for household wiring

questions.subject: chemistry

questions.subject: chemistry

solution.concept: 4.5 Non-metals such as nitrogen and phosphorus are used in fertilisers
steps: Plants need nitrogen and phosphorus (with potassium) for growth
Fertilisers such as urea and superphosphate supply them

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: A non-metal used in the purple solution applied on wounds as an antiseptic is

The copper set free coats the blade as a brown layer
